platform: Omarchy 4.5.0-3, Hyprland 0.56.2, kernel 7.2.15-1-omarchy, x86_64, Quickshell 0.3.2.r7, Node v26.13.0
scope: Live desktop acceptance of the 0.4.0 candidate: notifications gain three IPC-backed actions (Launch Loot Drops, Open Game Store, Mark as seen) for a single game, a per-store maxStoreNotifications cap (default 3, range 0-20) that bundles a store's batch into one summary whose only action opens the panel, and IPC methods openGame/markSeen. No rendering changed, so preview.png and the theme screenshots were not retaken. Portable checks, the 4.5 live shell, the IPC actions and the install/update/removal lifecycle were run.
install: The development symlink was unlinked (the repository untouched) and the plugin installed from https://github.com/salmun-nister/omarchy-loot-drops with `omarchy plugin add ... --enable --yes`, which cloned the 0.4.0 commit 928d93f. The clone was checked out at v0.3.1 to stand in for the previous release, the user's entry (amazonEnabled true, hideSeen true) was restored, and the shell restarted; `omarchy plugin update ... --yes` fast-forwarded to 928d93f. The shell.json entry kept both settings and seen.json stayed byte-identical (sha256 aac628ee...), so an update preserves settings and the stored-seen record, with the new maxStoreNotifications key falling back to its default. Removal then deleted the clone, unloaded the plugin and removed its entry while seen.json stayed byte-identical. The development symlink was re-linked, rescanned, enabled on the right, the original shell.json entry restored, and the plugin verified after a final restart. The IPC methods were exercised separately on the running 4.5 shell: marking a game seen through `markSeen epic <id>` changed the acknowledged set, and `openGame` rejected an unknown store and an invalid id without opening anything.
commands: omarchy-notification-send ... --action Launch Loot Drops ... --action Open Game Store ... --action Mark as seen ...
ln -s /home/kevin/Projects/Omarchy-Loot-Drops ~/.config/omarchy/plugins/salmun-nister.loot-drops; omarchy-shell shell rescanPlugins; omarchy plugin enable salmun-nister.loot-drops right
restore the original shell.json entry; omarchy restart shell

results.detail: ./tests/run passed 55 tests, the real Qt qmllint pass and the helper checks. validate_plugin.py reports valid with no errors or warnings and an advisory review-required security section; release_preflight.py reports READY with advisory matches only; omarchy plugin validate . exits 0. These are limited scans, not a security audit.

results.check: Notification actions and the per-store cap
results.detail: A single game's notification argv carries three --action entries in order — Launch Loot Drops (first, so the card click still opens the panel), Open Game Store, and Mark as seen — each calling omarchy-shell back into the widget with the store and a scrubbed id, so no URL or command rides in the notification. A bundled summary (more than one game) carries only Launch Loot Drops. The per-store cap normalises to 0-20 with a default of 3; 1 bundles any store batch and 0 removes the limit. All covered by the model tests.

results.check: Notification IPC actions on the live 4.5 shell
results.detail: With the candidate loaded after `omarchy restart shell`, `omarchy-shell -q salmun-nister.loot-drops markSeen epic 12de5cad...` changed seen.json: the id was absent from the Epic acknowledged set before the call and present after it, and the call exited 0, proving the shell forwards both arguments to the widget's IpcHandler and the widget persists the change. `openGame notastore x` and `openGame steam 'bad id'` both exited 0 without opening anything, confirming the validation path. A three-action test notification was sent on the live desktop; the agent cannot click or screenshot it, so the button rendering and clicks remain the user's to confirm.

./tests/harness/run against the live stores reported 28 rows across steam, epic, gog and amazon, with laid-out content and no QML errors. This is the transport and layout check, not a substitute for a desktop pass.

Installed from the repository URL at 928d93f (0.4.0), enabled in the right section and visible. The clone was checked out at v0.3.1, the user's settings restored, and `omarchy plugin update ... --yes` fast-forwarded to 928d93f; the shell.json entry kept amazonEnabled=true and hideSeen=true and seen.json stayed byte-identical. `omarchy plugin remove ... --yes` deleted the clone and unloaded the widget while seen.json stayed byte-identical. The development symlink and the original settings were restored and verified afterwards.

results.check: No preview or theme images changed
results.detail: This candidate changes notification construction and adds a setting, not panel rendering, so preview.png and the theme images were left as previously captured and are not part of this acceptance.

limitations: The notification buttons were not clicked by the agent: the open live panel pins the pointer and the agent cannot screenshot the desktop, so the three-button rendering and the Open Game Store browser launch are the user's to confirm. The IPC methods behind the buttons were exercised directly, and a test notification with all three actions was sent on 4.5. A multi-game bundled notification (a store over the cap) was not observed live because no refresh delivered more than the cap; the cap logic and both argv shapes are covered by portable tests. Live store contents vary, so a later fetch will not match the games named here. GOG's success path remains fixture-only because no giveaway was live. Amazon Luna's render was observed with its live games. A vertical bar has not been observed. Installing a clone removes the widget's shell.json settings, so the development symlink and this machine's settings were restored by hand after the lifecycle. No security audit is claimed; the validators are limited scans.
